Hazlo en 90 minutos, sin mirar las soluciones.
PAU 2027 · Modelo 2 de Escolapedia

Inglés II

Read the text and answer all the questions in English. Time: 90 minutes.

Nombre: ______________________   Fecha: ___________   Nota: ______

The real cost of cheap clothes

A T-shirt that costs less than a sandwich may seem like a bargain, but someone, somewhere, pays the difference. The fashion industry produces more than 100 billion items of clothing every year, and many of them are worn only a few times before being thrown away. This model, known as fast fashion, depends on low prices, constant new collections and the idea that clothes are disposable.

The environmental impact is huge. Producing a single pair of jeans can require thousands of litres of water, and synthetic fabrics release tiny plastic fibres every time they are washed. Most discarded clothes end up in landfills or are burned, while only a small percentage is actually recycled into new garments.

There are also human costs. Workers in some factories earn very low wages and work long hours in unsafe conditions. Yet many consumers, especially young people, are starting to change their habits. Second-hand apps have become popular, clothes-swapping events are organised in schools, and some brands now offer repair services. Buying less and choosing better, experts say, is the most sustainable option of all.

  1. TRUE or FALSE? Justify with evidence from the text. a) Most old clothes are recycled. b) Some young people are changing the way they buy clothes. c) Fast fashion relies on frequent new collections. (1,5 p.)

  2. Answer in your own words: a) Why is fast fashion bad for the environment? b) What alternatives does the text mention? (2 p.)

  3. Find words in the text that mean: a) something bought for a low price (par. 1); b) designed to be used once and then thrown away (par. 1); c) pieces of clothing (par. 2); d) payments for work (par. 3). (1 p.)

  4. Rewrite the sentences: a) Factories produce millions of clothes every year. → Millions of clothes… b) «I bought this jacket second-hand», she said. → She said that… c) If people bought less, the environment would suffer less. → Unless… (1,5 p.)

  5. Writing (120-150 words): Write an opinion essay: «Should schools teach students how to be responsible consumers?» (4 p.)

Soluciones y criterios de corrección

  1. a) FALSE: «only a small percentage is actually recycled». b) TRUE: «many consumers, especially young people, are starting to change their habits». c) TRUE: «depends on low prices, constant new collections…».
  2. a) Making clothes uses a lot of water, synthetic fabrics release microplastics when we wash them, and most clothes are thrown away and end up in landfills or burnt. b) Buying second-hand clothes through apps, exchanging clothes at school events, repairing clothes and, above all, buying fewer but better-quality items.
  3. a) bargain; b) disposable; c) garments; d) wages.
  4. a) Millions of clothes are produced (by factories) every year. b) She said that she had bought that jacket second-hand. c) Unless people bought less, the environment would suffer more. (Also accepted: «Unless people buy less, the environment will keep suffering».)
  5. Assessment: content (1), organisation (1), grammar (1), vocabulary (1). Good answers include an introduction stating the opinion, two developed reasons with examples (financial education, environmental awareness, critical thinking about advertising), a counter-argument (families should teach it / the timetable is already full) and a conclusion, with connectors such as Firstly, Furthermore, However, In conclusion.
